tl;dr - I keep getting ink on top of my pen nib. Is this normal?

Been wanting to get into the fountain pen world for a while now and the girlfriend just got me a Pilot Metro. I am loving the way it writes and how little pressure it requires to write with. I use it constantly throughout the day at my job. I do have one question though. I've noticed that ink does start to get on the top of the nib. I've tried wiping it but it seems like wiping it draws more ink out onto the nib. Is this normal for fountain pens to have some ink in this location? Do I have a problem with the pen leaking into the cap? The ink isn't getting on the barrel or transferring to the top of the pen when I place the lid on the pen while writing. I can't really find any info on this as asking anything about the nib just leads me to tons of articles on cleaning it.

It's called nib creep and is common on pretty much every pen. It is not a problem - and I think I might be worried if I had the opposite problem since that could bmean not enough ink was coming through the pen. I'll wipe it off if the pen was shaken and to much came out or ink has built up, but usually I leave it be. Its also a good way to show off your ink color!

You are asking a variation of the famous Cogito.

According to Descartes the only thing we can know with absolute certainty is the fact that we are capable of thinking and therefore the act of us thinking proves that we exist. By continuation of the same argument he says that everything else in the world may be merely an artifact of us thinking and can not be proven with certainty to exist outside of our thoughts. Your question is like a continuation of that argument.

"The only think I know with absolute certainty is that I am doing this thinking right now."

"I must exist because I am doing this thinking. I think therefore I am."

"Everything I think about could be a mere fiction of my thoughts, you, my arm, the universe, are just illusions that I've come up in my thinking. When I burn my finger on the flame, the pain is just an illusion of my imagination. I can't prove otherwise."

So the counter argument goes something like this:

"When you stub your toe on the foot of the chair does that hurt?"

"Yes but the pain is just a figment of my imagination, so is the chair."

"But you were not thinking about the chair when you stubbed your toe, it came as a surprise to you. Therefore the chair must exist even when you are not thinking about it."

"The fact that other things happen and affect you even when you are not thinking about them proves that they exist also"

And so on and so forth.
